correctness.rationale: Exact logistic and Gaussian CDFs reduce the claim to a scalar difference. The derivative sign is governed by R(c); R'(c) has a one-valley geometry because its derivative is strictly increasing after one curvature transition. Separated signs at c=0,1,2 and infinity yield exactly two derivative zeros. H(1)>0 and a three-term Mills bound gives H(2)<0, forcing exactly one positive crossing. The tail equivalent is exact logistic tail plus Mills asymptotic.
